observation.visible_scene: A rectangular step-cut (emerald/asscher-style) diamond stands tilted on a glossy black reflective surface, casting a sharp mirror-image reflection directly below it. The background is pure black with a few tiny dust-like sparkles scattered on the right side. The diamond remains centered in the frame throughout.
visible_changes: The diamond undergoes a slow rotation about its vertical axis: the orientation of its table and side facets changes gradually from frame 1 to frame 41, while its overall position in the frame stays essentially fixed (no translation).
The reflection below tracks the diamond's rotation and brightness changes, mirroring the same facet geometry.
A bright starburst flare ignites at the upper corner of the diamond around frames 12-16, peaks in frames 17-20, then fades out by frame 22.
Near the end (frames 33-41) a broad, bright light streak sweeps diagonally across the top of the diamond, accompanied by rainbow-colored lens flare artifacts.
A faint blue glow/flare appears and drifts in the left background from roughly frame 20 onward.
Internal facet brilliance shifts continuously as the diamond turns, with small colored (fire) flashes appearing on different facets.
outside_clip_unknowns: The lighting rig or turntable mechanism driving the rotation and flares is not visible.
Whether the rotation and flare sequence continue or stop after the last frame is unknown.
The exact cause of the background dust particles' slight movement is unseen.
uncertain_details: Rotation direction and speed are inferred only from gradual facet-orientation change; the motion is subtle and could partly reflect camera orbit rather than object spin.
The blue background glow and rainbow streaks are likely lens/optical artifacts rather than physical objects, but this cannot be confirmed.
The dust sparkles on the right may be floating particles or sensor noise; their motion is not clearly attributable.
